subject: EU / APAC private deployment: data placement & emergency failover authorization
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@acme-bank.com, eng@cloudpartner.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T15:12:00+00:00
Subject: EU / APAC private deployment: data placement & emergency failover authorization

Hi team,

Following our on-call tabletop last week, attaching the initial runbook draft for Acme Bank's private deployment residency and emergency failover between the EU and APAC VPCs. This thread is to get written authorization and an explicit list of acceptable failover conditions from Acme (procurement/legal) so we can formalize the operational controls.

Key points in the draft (high level):
- Primary site: EU (Frankfurt) — all persistent data and KMS keys provisioned in EU tenancy.
- Standby site: APAC (Singapore) — warm standby with cross-region replication of non-persistent caches and read-only artifacts only.
- Failover trigger types considered: full-region outage, sustained network egress blocking, catastrophic loss of EU region availability.
- Customer authorization model: two-tier approval (technical + legal/contract). We need a written acknowledgement from Acme that, in an emergency, Redwood may route workloads to APAC for continuity.
- Controls to minimize cross-border residency exposure: encrypted snapshots, per-tenant KMS keys, audit logs for any cross-region data movement.

Ask: procurement/legal — can Acme provide an explicit, time-bound authorization for emergency failover that includes (1) which data classes may be relocated temporarily, (2) max dwell/exposure time, and (3) KMS / key export constraints?

Jonas / Marcus — please review the networking and KMS sections and call out anything missing (peering, egress ACLs, short TTL cert rotation, BGP failover notes).

Attachments: acme-residency-failover-draft.pdf (runbook draft)

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Site Reliability (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-bank.com, eng@cloudpartner.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T18:04:00+00:00
Subject: Re: EU / APAC private deployment: data placement & emergency failover authorization

Hannah — quick technical notes / gaps I see in the draft:

1) Network and peering:
- Ensure VPC peering is one-way (EU -> APAC) for replication path; block primary-originated egress from APAC to EU unless explicitly approved.
- Use route table tags per-tenant so we can revoke cross-region routes for a specific customer quickly.

2) KMS & keys:
- Do NOT export EU-managed customer keys to APAC. Instead, use envelope keys: the DEK (data encryption key) is replicated encrypted with the EU KEK (key encryption key) and APAC holds a KEK that can be used only after explicit legal/contract unlock.
- Add a manual unlock flow and an automated failover flow: manual unlock requires signed confirmation; automated flow triggers only if we detect region-level service degradation > 15 minutes AND legal opt-in is present.

3) Audit & telemetry:
- Add an immutable audit event that records what objects moved, who authorized, and the signed PDF grant from the customer.
- Retention: store the audit events in EU-only log buckets; replicate a redacted index to APAC for troubleshooting.

4) Routing failback:
- Post-failover, we run a staged backfill to move persisted data back to EU; this must be scheduled as low-priority and can be throttled.

I can update the runbook with network diagrams and the KEK/DEK flow if Hannah wants.

— Jonas
Senior Network Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Acme Bank Procurement <procurement@acme-bank.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, eng@cloudpartner.com
Date: 2026-10-19T09:23:00+00:00
Subject: Re: EU / APAC private deployment: data placement & emergency failover authorization

Hannah / Jonas — thanks for the draft. A few items we need clarified before legal can sign off:

- Explicit data classes: we require a list that maps Redwood data types to our taxonomy (Customer PII, Financial Transaction Logs, Aggregates). Only Aggregates are allowed to be processed in APAC under emergency authorization; PII and Transaction Logs must remain in EU unless data is irretrievably required for continuity and a documented escalation path is followed.
- Max exposure window: our default is 72 hours unless we pre-authorize extensions.
- Proof of controls: provide SOC2 evidence for the APAC site and an attestation that APAC KMS is in a physically separate HSM.
- Contract amendment: procurement needs a short addendum that includes the authorization model and rollback SLA (RTO/RPO expectations).

We can provide a one-page authorization template if you want — procurement@acme-bank.com. Please include the explicit paths for manual authorization so we can map to our internal approval flow.

Regards,
Clara Jensen
Head of Procurement, Acme Bank
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@acme-bank.com, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, eng@cloudpartner.com
Date: 2026-10-20T11:35:00+00:00
Subject: Re: EU / APAC private deployment: data placement & emergency failover authorization

Clara / team — thank you, noted. I updated the runbook to incorporate Acme's requested constraints and the authorization template you offered. Attached: acme-residency-failover-v1.1.pdf (runbook + one-page authorization template). Summary of what changed:

- Data class mapping table added (PII / Transactions / Aggregates) and explicit statement that only Aggregates are eligible for automatic APAC routing.
- Exposure window default set to 48 hours with a documented extension workflow (customer-signed extension via DocuSign).
- New section: KMS handling — KEK in EU HSM; APAC KEK sealed and requires customer signed unlock or mutual-auth token for automated unlock.
- Added list of required evidence: APAC SOC2 cert, HSM attestation, network ACL snapshots.
- DocuSign link for the one-page emergency authorization included below.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/sign/EXAMPLE-ACM-2026-014
Drive runbook: https://drive.redwood.internal/docs/ACM-2026-014/residency-runbook

Next steps:
- Acme procurement/legal: review v1.1 and either sign the one-page authorization or send redlines by COB Friday.
- Jonas / Marcus: prepare the KEK sealing runbook and network revocation play (I need both before we enable standby routing in the tenant).

Thanks,
Hannah
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-bank.com, eng@cloudpartner.com
Date: 2026-10-20T16:45:00+00:00
Subject: Re: EU / APAC private deployment: data placement & emergency failover authorization

Hannah — reviewed the updated runbook. I approve proceeding to procurement with v1.1, contingent on two additions before we flip any tenant-level routing flags:

1) Add an SLA exception clause that quantifies the rollback window (target RPO = 15m for in-flight state; target RTO = 60m for full service).
2) Add the retention/erasure step: any persisted data in APAC after failback must be cryptographically shredded within 30 days unless customer explicitly extends.

Marcus — please coordinate the change list with Jonas and confirm when the KEK sealing procedures are ready; copy me on the final internal checklist. Once those are green, Hannah can request the signed DocuSign from Acme and we move to operational readiness.

— Lauren
VP, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
